hypotheses.paper: def:semi_locally_simple_connectedness (l.1451): X Hausdorff, connected, locally path-connected
hypotheses.note: the witness satisfies all three and is moreover compact and metrizable (a Peano continuum); the refutation statement quantifies over T2, connected, locally path-connected, compact X
both the literal DEC-55 form GX.IsSLSCInCC univ and the homotopy form GX.IsSLSCIn univ are proved for the witness
GX.SemilocallySimplyConnected (DEC-41), the notion the archipelago counterexample of GX.Branched.Galois refutes

findings: RamcovGX.tex:1455-1457: the printed 'iff' fails even among compact metrizable spaces. The Griffiths twin cone (the cones over two Hawaiian earrings, apexes (±1/2, 1), wedged at the earrings' common point; GX.GriffithsSpace in ℂ × ℝ = ℝ³) is compact, Hausdorff, path-connected, locally path-connected, semi-locally simply connected in itself in the literal DEC-55 sense and in the homotopy sense, and not semi-locally simply connected (GX.griffiths_counterexample; the refuted statement with compactness added is GX.not_semilocallySimplyConnected_of_isSLSCInCC_univ_compact). No compactness hypothesis rescues the converse; only slsc ⇒ slsc in itself holds (GX.isSLSCInCC_univ_of_semilocallySimplyConnected, GX.Branched.Galois).

Why it is slsc in itself: off 0 a point has a star-shaped neighbourhood inside one cone; at 0 a loop below the apexes slides down the cone lines onto the double earring, and the finitely many circles of index < N contract through their cones (GX.grifColl), so every such loop is homotopic rel endpoints into the 2/N-ball. Why it is not slsc: the loops ∏_{n≥N} a_n b_n lie in the 2/N-ball and are not null-homotopic. The proof is self-contained, not Griffiths' original. It uses the linking matrix Z_ij of a loop of the double earring (GX.grifZ, a homotopy-invariant crossed homomorphism). Modulo the integer matrices of finite rank, Z is a homomorphism (GX.grifTheta) that vanishes on each earring and equals the infinite unitriangular matrix on ∏ a_n b_n. Two Seifert–van Kampen gluings of GX.VanKampen.Data, one per apex, extend it to all loops.

Mathematical remark, NOT formalized: a counterexample to the converse cannot be homotopically Hausdorff at the bad point. If every loop of V at x is homotopic into every neighbourhood of x, and only null-homotopic loops are, then every loop of V is null-homotopic. Conversely, slsc implies homotopically Hausdorff. So in the homotopy reading, 'X slsc ⇔ X slsc in itself and homotopically Hausdorff' would be a true corrected form of the remark. This is offered to the author, not proved here.
questions: DEC-135 asked for a compact counterexample besides the harmonic archipelago. The Griffiths twin cone is one, and a Peano continuum. Both witnesses refute the same direction. Reading taken: both are kept, the archipelago in GX.Branched.Galois and the twin cone here; the row stays partial (DEC-27). Which one anchors the row's finding is the author's choice.

kb_proposals: pitfall: `rw` fails ('motive is not type correct' at instances transparency) when path endpoints are defeq but not syntactic (`D.x₀` vs a named point, `↑⟨q, h⟩` vs `q`). State restrictions with syntactic endpoints (a dedicated restriction def, cf. `GX.grifSub`), chain equalities with `Eq.trans`/`refine` instead of `rw`, and push `Subtype.val` through `Path.trans_apply` with `apply_dite Subtype.val` before `split_ifs` (T-gx-slsc-compact).

pattern: `GX.VanKampen.Data.Φ` is multiplicative (`GX.VanKampen.Data.Φ_trans`), so a glued invariant can be glued again: one gluing per bad point, the base point moved by conjugation along a tether (`GX.grifD1`, `GX.grifD2`); `GX.grifMkData` builds the data from three path-connected opens and an invariant on `U` that is trivial on `U ∩ V`.

pattern: an infinitesimal non-null loop (homotopic into every neighbourhood, as in Griffiths-type spaces) is invisible to every continuous invariant valued in a homotopically Hausdorff target. Detect it with a homotopy invariant valued in a quotient group, e.g. the linking matrix modulo finite rank (`GX.grifTheta`), built from exp-lifts and winding numbers (`GX.cWinding`).
